editorial:
Imagine going to a school where you can get in huge trouble just for having brown hair. That is the crazy world you enter here. You will meet Sora, a quiet kid who blends into the background, and Chūya, who is basically a wild card. Both of them are crushing on Kio, a girl who refuses to dye her natural hair black just to please the school. Since the rules are so strict, Kio stops coming to class entirely. It is a sweet but frustrating setup that makes you root for the underdogs to take down a system that cares more about hair color than actual learning.

You will love how the friendship between the boys evolves as they fight the administration. The acting feels very real, and the pacing keeps you interested without feeling too slow. While some parts are a bit predictable, the emotional payoff is great. If you enjoy stories about teens standing up for what is right, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, Sora and Chūya lead a successful movement to change the unfair rules. They manage to convince the school and other students that hair color does not matter. Because of their hard work, the rule is finally dropped, and Kio is allowed to return to class without dyeing her hair. The movie wraps up with a feeling of victory, showing that even the quietest students can make a big difference when they team up.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and school rebels.
